question: What does ordinary MLP activity in Qwen3-4B look like: a few single neurons at a time, a few large low-dimensional modes (shapes/subspaces), or many mid-sized assemblies? Descriptive census with shuffle nulls.
data: Qwen3-4B bf16 on the 80 FineWeb-Edu documents used for the tower's co-fire map (19,430 tokens), all 36 layers, every MLP neuron's activation (down_proj input), each neuron scaled by its own corpus range (corpus_all.npz) as the tower does.

measures.M1_sparsity: per token and layer: how many neurons exceed 0.5 / 0.25 of their own range; share of the layer's total |activation| carried by the top 1 / 10 / 100 neurons. 'Single-neuron' regime = top-10 carry most of the mass.
measures.M2_dimensionality: per layer, on a fixed random 2,000-neuron sample: PCA over tokens; participation ratio and number of components for 50/90% variance; vs a SHUFFLE null (each neuron's time series permuted independently, which keeps every neuron's own distribution and kills co-activation). Collective structure = real PR far below shuffled PR.
measures.M3_collective_share: variance explained by the top 10 PCs, real vs shuffled - how much activity is shared modes vs independent.
measures.M4_persistence: autocorrelation of the active set across tokens (Jaccard of top-1% sets at lag 1/4/16): token-level flicker vs phrase-level states.
measures.M5_vertical: canonical correlation between adjacent-layer top-10 PC scores and between layers 8 apart: are modes threads through the tower (like the assemblies) or per-floor?

predictions_written_before: P1: per token, top-10 neurons carry < 20% of a layer's mass (not a single-neuron regime). P2: real participation ratio < 1/3 of shuffled in mid layers (strong shared modes). P3: Jaccard at lag 1 > 3x lag 16 (phrase-level persistence).
notes: Runs on mini-mini (16 GB): stream statistics per layer, never the full token x 350k matrix. Outputs gitignored.

stage_2_steered.question: How does a steering push travel? Does the change it causes ride the model's natural (census) modes or go off-manifold, how far up the tower does it reach, and does spreading a push across floors help?
stage_2_steered.conditions: base; void L21N8400 -40; alien L10N5045 -32; semiconductor L10N6249 +40; random neuron at the void's push norm (control); spread arm: the void's direction split over floors 19..23 at 1/5 dose each.
stage_2_steered.method: 20 identity prompts; each condition is fed the SAME text (the base model's own reply, teacher-forced) so activation changes are token-matched. MLP activations (scaled by corpus range) on a fixed 1,000-neuron sample per floor; natural PCs per floor from 30 FineWeb-Edu docs.
stage_2_steered.measures: per floor: mean |delta| and count of neurons with |delta| > .25 range; share of delta variance inside the top-10 natural PCs vs a random 10-d subspace (on-manifold index); for the seed conditions, overlap of the 100 most-changed sampled neurons... (sample-limited) replaced by: full-floor top-100 changed neurons vs the seed's top-20 weight neighbours, co-fire partners (cofire.npz) and assemblies. Spread arm also generates freely (60 tokens) scored with the persona-cluster D2 readout for the void.
stage_2_steered.predictions: P1: the push's change grows or holds above the injection floor (not decaying) for the persona seeds. P2: on-manifold index of seed pushes exceeds the random-neuron control (the personas ride natural modes). P3: the spread arm reaches >= the single-floor void hits at equal total norm with fewer incoherent replies.
